newsitem.title: USA: Hashimoto, Clinton say they agree on trade goals.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto, Clinton say they agree on trade goals.

text.p: President Clinton and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said Friday they agreed that Japan should promote strong domestic demand-led growth and avoid a significant rise in Japan's trade surplus.

"We both want to promote strong domestic demand-led growth in Japan, and to avoid a significant increase in Japan's external surplus," Clinton said at a news conference with Hashimoto following talks between the two leaders.
"We both support the common objective of avoiding a significant increase in Japan's external surplus by supporting strong domestic demand-led growth in Japan," Hashimoto said.

U.S. officials have expressed concern in recent weeks that gains made last year in reducing the huge trade imbalance between the two countries will be reversed. They have urged Japan not to try to export its way out of recession.

Clinton and Hashimoto also said they agreed to intensify talks on Tokyo's deregulation efforts. U.S. officials want to ensure that Japan's deregulation efforts will help open its markets up to more foreign-made goods.
The economic relationship was one of a number of issues discussed by the two leaders during three hours of formal talks at the White House on Friday. The two met informally Thursday night.
